architectural-decision-records.why: records the opt-in code-owner-review decision and its honest limit
architectural-decision-records.what: wrote ADR 0055: esk-genesis --code-owners scaffolds CODEOWNERS over the enforcement paths (no-clobber, fail-closed), prints the one-time ruleset setting it cannot make, and the bootstrap skill asks the user (D4)
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

verifiable-quality-gates.why: the flow ships discriminating tests that go red if it stops scaffolding or stops failing closed
verifiable-quality-gates.what: added tests: --code-owners scaffolds CODEOWNERS over the paths, absent flag writes nothing, an existing file is not clobbered, an invalid owner blocks with nothing written
quotes: replace each check with a no-op and require its test to fail

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: the change adds executable logic, so the test level is explicit
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: fixture-driven tests run the real generator with and without the flag, over an existing file, and with an invalid owner; the right level for a scaffolding generator
quotes: Fast, isolated tests for logic; a smaller number of integration tests for the seams

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: coupling fires on the added code; the behavior is pinned as scenarios
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: implements opt-in CODEOWNERS scaffolding and the ask-the-user flow, with discriminating scenarios for present/absent/existing/invalid
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment. Every time this

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: the generator writes owner handles into a committed CODEOWNERS file
owasp-secure-coding-bdd.what: each owner is validated against @user / @org/team before being written, so a malformed or injected token is a blocker not a file write; an existing CODEOWNERS is never overwritten
quotes: For the change in front of you, look up the matching sheet in the catalog below

skeptical-audit.why: the ADR and the output state what it does NOT do
skeptical-audit.what: documented that committing CODEOWNERS is necessary but NOT sufficient, that the installer cannot enable the require-code-owner-review ruleset rule, and that the file is inert until a human turns it on
quotes: content hash, a query, a version/commit SHA, or a URL + retrieval date;

judge-arch.why: reviewed in fresh context before the PR
judge-arch.what: ran a fresh-context judge-arch over the --code-owners flow, the scaffold write, the skill guidance, and the ADR before opening the PR
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all

release-deployment-safety.why: a setup-time scaffold; nothing deployed, migrated, or released

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: CI/dev tooling; no system, data, or resilience architecture change

pattern-selector.why: no design pattern selected; a scaffold plus a guard

sre-operational-readiness.why: no service, SLI/SLO, or alerting change

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: owner handles are repo governance metadata, not personal data under management

arch-encode.why: a feature, not a rule encoded from a newly-caught mistake

usability-ux-universal-design.why: agent guidance text, not a user-facing UI
